key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search identified 58 CuI-based ternary compounds as promising p-type transparent conductors, revealing 49 new candidates and four general design rules for halide-based CMVB systems.
engineering_relevance: These materials and design rules expand the search space for transparent p-type layers relevant to transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaic device stacks.
method: Minima hopping structure search over X–Cu–I ternaries
Density functional theory screening for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass
Revisit of chemical modulation of the valence band descriptors for Cu-based halide systems
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 58 candidate p-type TCMs, including 20 degenerate semiconductors with intrinsic holes, and highlights Cu2FI2 with a 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m0 hole effective mass.
watch_item: The results are computationally screened candidates, so experimental synthesis, phase stability under growth conditions, and device-level transparency/conductivity still need validation.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
